title: Where Would You Live?
big_idea: Every place has its own words, but the best words are the ones two places share.

regions.why: Words that belong to busy city life.

words.meaning: a train that runs under the ground
words.example: I take the subway to work every morning.

words.meaning: many cars and buses on the road
words.example: The traffic downtown is terrible at five o'clock.

words.meaning: a home inside a big building
words.example: Her apartment is on the tenth floor.

words.meaning: to travel to work or school every day
words.example: I commute forty minutes each way.

words.meaning: full of too many people
words.example: The sidewalk was so crowded I couldn't walk.

words.meaning: the shape of tall buildings against the sky
words.example: The skyline looks amazing at night.

words.meaning: when roads are too full to move well
words.example: Congestion pricing cut traffic in the center.

words.meaning: when richer people move in and old residents can't pay
words.example: Gentrification pushed rents up across the neighborhood.

words.meaning: full of people and ideas from many countries
words.example: Boston feels cosmopolitan because of all the students.

regions.why: Words for farms, fields and quiet places.

words.meaning: land where people grow food or keep animals
words.example: My uncle has a farm with twenty cows.

words.meaning: a big farm animal that gives milk
words.example: The cows walked slowly across the field.

words.meaning: an open area of grass or crops
words.example: We had a picnic in the field.

words.meaning: the time when farmers collect crops
words.example: Everyone helps during the apple harvest.

words.meaning: a farm building for animals or hay
words.example: The horses sleep in the red barn.

words.meaning: of the countryside, not the city
words.example: She grew up in a rural town of 800 people.

words.meaning: calm and peaceful, like country life
words.example: The painting shows a pastoral scene with sheep.

words.meaning: far away from other people
words.example: They rented a secluded cabin in the hills.

words.meaning: about farming and land
words.example: The region still has an agrarian economy.

regions.why: Words for sand, waves and the sea.

words.meaning: tiny pieces of rock on the beach
words.example: The sand was too hot for bare feet.

words.meaning: to move through water using your body
words.example: We swim in the ocean every summer.

words.meaning: moving water that rises and falls
words.example: A big wave knocked me over.

words.meaning: cream that protects skin from the sun
words.example: Put on sunscreen before you go outside.

words.meaning: the land along the edge of the sea
words.example: We walked along the shore at sunset.

words.meaning: a person who keeps swimmers safe
words.example: The lifeguard blew her whistle at the kids.

words.meaning: water under the waves that pulls away from shore
words.example: The undertow is strong here, so stay close.

words.meaning: slowly wearing land away with water or wind
words.example: Erosion is shrinking the beach every year.

words.meaning: about the sea rising and falling each day
words.example: Tidal pools fill with crabs at low tide.

regions.why: Things you find in both town and country, but not at the beach.

words.meaning: a way for cars to travel
words.example: The road into town is long and straight.

words.meaning: a place where children learn
words.example: The school is next to the library.

words.meaning: a place to buy and sell things
words.example: We buy eggs at the Saturday market.

words.meaning: a person who lives near you
words.example: Our neighbor fed the cat while we were away.

words.meaning: buses and trains anyone can use
words.example: Public transport is easy in the city and rare in the country.

words.meaning: rules about what can be built where
words.example: Zoning stops factories near houses.

words.meaning: roads, power, water and other basic systems
words.example: Rural infrastructure needs more money.

words.meaning: run by a town or city government
words.example: The municipal pool opens in June.

words.meaning: the area where a government has power
words.example: The farm is outside the city's jurisdiction.

regions.why: Busy, fun and touristy: city and beach together.

words.meaning: a building where travelers pay to sleep
words.example: Our hotel was across from the beach.

words.meaning: a place where you pay to eat
words.example: The restaurant serves fresh fish.

words.meaning: full of people and activity
words.example: The boardwalk gets busy in July.

words.meaning: a person visiting a place for fun
words.example: Tourists fill the streets every summer.

words.meaning: bars, clubs and fun things to do at night
words.example: Miami is famous for its nightlife.

words.meaning: something you buy to remember a trip
words.example: I bought a shell necklace as a souvenir.

words.meaning: the part of a town next to the water
words.example: The waterfront is lined with cafes.

words.meaning: busy and full of energy
words.example: The bustling harbor never sleeps.

words.meaning: with too many buildings
words.example: Locals say the coast is overdeveloped.

regions.why: Nature and open sky: country and beach together.

words.meaning: with very little noise
words.example: It's so quiet you can hear the birds.

words.meaning: small lights in the night sky
words.example: Away from the city you can see the stars.

words.meaning: clean air outside
words.example: I need some fresh air after the long drive.

words.meaning: animals living in nature
words.example: The dunes are full of wildlife.

words.meaning: a small, simple wooden house
words.example: We rented a cabin near the lake and the sea.

words.meaning: the natural things you see around you
words.example: The scenery on the coast road is beautiful.

words.meaning: still natural and not changed by people
words.example: It's one of the last unspoiled beaches.

words.meaning: calm and peaceful
words.example: The tranquil morning was perfect for reading.

words.meaning: all living things in one area working together
words.example: Wetlands are a fragile ecosystem.

regions.why: Words that work anywhere you live.

words.meaning: the place where you live
words.example: Home can be a city flat or a beach shack.

words.meaning: rain, sun, wind and temperature
words.example: Everyone talks about the weather.

words.meaning: to move on foot
words.example: I walk my dog wherever I live.

words.meaning: the people who live in one place
words.example: A strong community helps people feel safe.

words.meaning: money you pay every month to live somewhere
words.example: Rent is cheaper outside the city.

words.meaning: the way a person usually lives
words.example: Moving changed my whole lifestyle.

words.meaning: how much money you need to live in a place
words.example: The cost of living decides where many people move.

words.meaning: the feeling that you fit in a place
words.example: A sense of belonging matters more than the view.

words.meaning: useful things nearby, like shops and parks
words.example: The town lacks basic amenities like a pharmacy.
